steps.title: Linear bearings into the carriage
steps.note: 2 from below, 2 from above, flush with the faces
steps.fit: LM6UU into the carriage ×4: ~Ø12.25 as printed (13.3 in CAD, teardrop pockets: no support inside). Each bearing should slide in by hand. Loose: one wrap of electrical tape round the bearing. Tight: sandpaper on a dowel. Old carriage (pockets ~12.0 with support bits inside): clear the bits with a small screwdriver, then sand, or reprint.
steps.how: Do this on the table, carriage on its own: 2 bearings from below, 2 from above, flush with the faces. No glue (a drop of superglue only if one is loose and tape doesn't hold). The bearings are optional for a first test: the carriage also slides on the bare rods, with more friction (see step 7).

callouts.text: pocket ~Ø12.25 printed · slides in; loose: tape

steps.title: Lift link onto the carriage
steps.note: Pivot screw into the carriage's small boss: snug, then back off ¼ turn so the link swings
steps.fit: This joint must turn. The link's big hole is the pivot: it must swing freely on the screw (open it with a 5/32″ bit by hand if it binds).
steps.how: Carriage on the table, nothing else on it yet. Lay the link's big hole over the carriage's small boss and drive ONE #6 × ¼″ pointed (sheet-metal) pan-head screw in sideways. Stop as soon as it is snug, then back off ¼ turn so the link swings. Use a ¼″ screw, not ½″: a longer one reaches the rod's path.

callouts.text: #6 × ¼″ pointed · link must swing (5/32″ bit)

steps.title: Lift servo into the spine
steps.note: Spine on its own: servo body through the bracket from the left, 2 tab screws
steps.how: Spine on the table on its own. Push the lift servo's body through the spine's bracket from the left until its tabs sit on the bracket, then 2 servo-bag screws through the tabs. Its spline points left, out of the spine.

steps.title: Crank: horn on the link, then on the lift servo
steps.note: Screw the link's free end onto the horn's 20 mm hole FIRST, then press the horn onto the servo at 30° + centre screw
steps.fit: The link must turn on the crank screw. Open the link's small hole to 3/32″ (2.4 mm) so the screw only bites the horn. The servo now swings 68° (LIFT_UP 98): the carriage rises 15.7 mm.
steps.how: Do it in this order, everything still on the table: 1) Set the lift servo to 30° (laptop panel). 2) Take the single-arm horn from the servo bag (don't cut it) and screw the link's small hole onto its LAST hole (~14 mm from the centre): a servo-bag screw through the link into the horn. 3) Hold the carriage + link + horn up to the spine and press the horn onto the servo spline with the arm pointing toward the rods, tilted ~34° below horizontal (the nearest spline tooth; fine-tune LIFT_DOWN / LIFT_UP in the laptop panel). 4) The small centre screw through the horn into the spline. Now spine, servo, crank, link and carriage hang together.

steps.title: Turret plate + turntable horn (on the table)
steps.note: Horn under the plate, inside the hub; 4 screws down through the plate into the horn
steps.how: On the table, before anything else is on the plate: put the MG996R round horn under the turret plate, inside the hub, its 4 inner holes lined up with the plate's 4 small holes. Drive 4 servo-bag screws DOWN through the plate into the horn (open the plate's 4 holes to 3/32″ / 2.4 mm first so the screws pull the plate onto the horn). The plate and horn are now one part: they go onto the servo at the very end (step 19).

steps.title: Spine onto the turret plate
steps.note: The spine (with servo, crank, link and carriage hanging on it) onto the plate behind the rod holes, 2 screws from above
steps.how: Stand the spine (with the lift servo, crank, link and carriage hanging on it) on the turret plate behind the 2 rod holes. 2 × #6-32 from ABOVE through the spine's foot into the plate. Each screw head sits in a small half-round notch in the spine wall (old spine without the notch: file or Dremel a 1.5 mm half-round notch next to each hole, or use a #6 screw with a smaller head).

steps.title: Rods down through the carriage into the plate
steps.note: Hold the carriage level; each rod down through both its bearings into its blind hole in the plate
steps.fit: Rod ends into the turret plate: ~Ø5.95 as printed (7.05 in CAD): light press, straight down to the bottom. Too tight: open with a 15/64″ (5.95 mm) bit turned by hand. Then the slide test: Tilt the rods: the carriage must slide down by its own weight with no tight spot. Sticks: the tight pocket needs a little sanding. Without bearings it slides too, but needs ~1.5 N more from the lift servo and the printed bore wears in time.
steps.how: Hold the carriage level over the rod holes. Push each rod down from the top: through the carriage's upper bearing, its lower bearing, then into its blind hole in the turret plate, all the way to the bottom. No screws, no glue: the top cap traps the rods next.

callouts.text: blind hole ~Ø5.95 printed · 15/64″ bit if tight

steps.title: Top cap
steps.note: Over the rod tops onto the spine. Carriage still slides freely?
steps.fit: Try-fit, both rods (~Ø5.95 as printed). Old cap: holes drilled 15/64″ by hand, 8 mm deep. Then the 2 screws. After: the carriage must still slide freely.
steps.how: 2 × #6-32 from ABOVE through the cap into the top of the spine. The cap holds the rod tops in line (they can't come out of the plate) and ties the spine to the rods into one stiff frame. Drilling the cap's rod holes right through is fine: a rod a little too long then just sticks out.

callouts.text: blind hole ~Ø5.95 · 15/64″ bit if tight, 8 mm deep

steps.title: Gripper frame onto the wrist horn (on the table)
steps.note: Horn flat on the frame's flange, 4 screws through the flange into the horn
steps.how: On the table: the wrist servo's cross horn (4 arms, from the bag) flat on the gripper frame's flange, hub centred on the flange. Drill 1/16″ pilots through 4 of the horn's holes (one per arm, ~6 mm from the centre) into the flange, then 4 servo-bag screws. Using the horn as the drill guide means the holes always line up, whatever horn you have.

steps.title: Both fingers, gears meshed
steps.note: Slide them in together between the plates, open by the same angle
steps.fit: Gear mesh: try it on. Teeth engage with a little play and no binding over the full swing. Never sand or file gear teeth. Printers rarely print teeth exactly, so the file is made to be edited: if they bind, print the looser pair (cad/print/stl/finger_variants/, gear_thin 0.18 or 0.25); if they rattle, the tighter pair (0.00). Or set gear_thin in backend/cad/model.py and run backend/cad/finger_variants.py.
steps.how: Slide both fingers in together between the plates, both opened by the same angle, so the teeth mesh symmetrically.

steps.title: Right finger axle
steps.note: From the top through the right finger; it must swing freely
steps.fit: Ø3.9 mm running fit. The finger must swing freely on the axle. Tight: twist a 5/32 in drill through by hand.
steps.how: #6-32 from the top through the frame and the right finger, threading into the bottom plate: it is the axle.

steps.title: Horn on the left gear, then the gripper servo
steps.note: Horn flat on the left gear, 2 screws; then the servo's spline down into the horn hub
steps.fit: Horn trimmed to Ø12 mm, flat on the gear. Cut the SG90 round horn down to Ø12 mm (flush cutters, then sand), keeping its 2 holes 5 mm from the centre (or drill 1.5 mm through the horn using the gear's pilots as the guide). A full-size horn hits the servo post. The spline must slide into the hub without force.
steps.how: Take the double-arm horn from the SG90 bag and cut both arms off 7 mm from the centre (flush cutters or the rotary tool's cut-off disc): it must turn inside the frame's 16 mm opening. Lay it flat on the left gear, hub up and centred; drill 1/16″ pilots through its 2 remaining holes into the gear and drive 2 servo-bag screws. Then the SG90: its spline goes down into the horn's hub, 2 tab screws into the posts.

callouts.text: horn screws → 2 small holes, 5 mm from centre

steps.title: Wrist servo into the arm
steps.note: Body through the arm's bracket from the front, 2 tab screws
steps.how: Body through the arm's bracket from the front, 2 servo-bag screws through the tabs.

steps.title: Claw onto the wrist servo
steps.note: Press the wrist horn (with the whole claw on it) onto the servo spline, plates level
steps.how: Wrist servo at 0° first. Hold the whole claw (frame + horn + fingers + gripper servo) with the plates level and press the horn's hub onto the wrist servo's spline until it is fully on. No centre screw: the frame covers it, and the spline teeth carry the turning force.

steps.title: Can bumper
steps.note: Silicone or rubber, 9 × 13.5 mm, superglue to the frame
steps.how: Cut 9 x 13.5 mm from the silicone sheet (or a rubber band / inner tube).
steps.glue_text: Superglue the rubber pad to the frame where the can's side touches.

steps.title: Bearing into the base
steps.note: Press on the outer ring only, evenly (flat block + vise)
steps.fit: 6807 into the base pocket: ~Ø47.0 as printed (48.0 in the CAD file; this printer makes holes ~1 mm small). Old base (46.0): open it with a sanding drum, low speed, all the way round, to 47.0. Too tight: sand the wall a little at a time. Loose: 1 layer of tape on the bearing.
steps.how: Push on the OUTER ring only, evenly: flat block on top, squeeze in a vise or press with both thumbs. No glue.

callouts.text: pocket ~Ø47.0 printed · sand the wall to fit

steps.title: Turntable servo
steps.note: From underneath; body points away from the arm side
steps.fit: Spline height. A base printed before 25 Nov has its 2 servo mounting blocks 5 mm too long (the CAD had the MG996R 5 mm too tall): sand 5 mm off the blocks' bottom faces, both equally, so the spline reaches the horn under the turret plate. New base files are already corrected.
steps.how: 4 x #8-32 screws from UNDERNEATH: through the 4 holes in the servo's tabs, up into the 2 printed blocks inside the base. They cut their own thread in the plastic: snug, don't over-tighten (it strips).

steps.title: Weight + feet
steps.note: ~100 g in the 2 back pockets (washers, pennies, rocks, a bag of sand): GLUE or TAPE it in. 4 feet or hot-glue dots
steps.how: ~50 g of washers / coins / small rocks in each back pocket, glued in. Optional: 4 rubber feet or hot-glue dots under the base. A bag of sand or a handful of washers works as the weight.
steps.glue_text: Hot glue or tape the washers into the 2 back pockets: the pockets are open underneath, loose weight just stays on the table.

steps.title: Column onto the turntable servo
steps.note: Servo at 135° first. Hub into the bearing, horn onto the spline, rod side toward the START can
steps.fit: Hub into the 6807's inner ring: ~Ø34.9 as printed (34.3 in CAD). It should press in by hand and the plate must turn freely after. Too tight: sand the hub evenly while turning it. Loose: one wrap of tape on the hub.
steps.how: Turntable servo at 135° first (laptop panel: Base 135). Lower the whole column straight down: the turret plate's hub goes into the bearing's inner ring and the horn (already screwed under the plate) onto the servo's spline; turn the column until the spline teeth engage, rod side facing the START can. No centre screw: the column covers it; its weight keeps the horn on the spline and the bearing carries the load. Check: the column turns smoothly by hand when the servo is unpowered.

callouts.text: hub ~Ø34.9 printed · loose: tape / tight: sand

steps.title: Electronics on the tray
steps.note: Pegs + a dab of hot glue; breadboard is self-adhesive. Buck already set to 5.8 V
steps.how: Boards onto the printed pegs. Buck already set to 5.8 V (bench test).
steps.glue_text: A dab of hot glue on each peg holds the Uno and the buck. The breadboard is self-adhesive.

steps.title: Panel: button, LED, power
steps.note: Through the panel holes from the front, nuts inside. Power: DC jack, or the LIZVOR terminal-block tip
steps.how: Button, LED and DC jack go through the panel holes from the front; their nuts go on inside.

steps.title: Tray onto the base
steps.note: Tabs slide under the base wall, screws from below
steps.how: Tabs slide under the base wall, then 2 x #6-32 from UNDERNEATH through the tabs into the base.

names.lift_crank: Single-arm horn, from the bag, last hole
names.gripper_horn: SG90 double-arm horn, arms cut to 7 mm

precise.label: PRECISE FIT
precise.text: Press fits and alignment that decide whether the robot works (steps 1, 7, 16, 19). The holes are now corrected for this printer; test each fit with the real part, tape if loose, sand if tight.

try.label: TRY-FIT
try.text: Test before you tighten: it should turn, slide or mesh freely. Easy to fix with a drill bit by hand, a knife or sandpaper.

easy.label: EASY
easy.text: Screws into servo tabs, glue, boards on pegs. Any print quality works: do these while other parts are still printing.

while_waiting: Electronics bench test (PART E) and set the buck to 5.8 V
Set every servo to its angle (laptop panel) before it gets its horn
Cut the 2 rods to 112 mm, file the ends
Find the horns in the servo bags: single-arm (lift, step 4), cross (wrist, step 9), double-arm cut to 7 mm (gripper, step 12)
Cut the rubber pad 9 x 13.5 mm (step 15)
Build the whole column on the table (steps 1-15) while the base prints: it goes onto the base in step 19
